t.7.74.1: Having heard that speech of Rāma, whose deeds were unwearied, the doorkeeper summoned the two princes and announced them to Rāghava.
t.7.74.2: Seeing his dear Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa arrived, Rāghava embraced them, and then Rāma spoke these words.
t.7.74.3: The supreme task on behalf of the brahmin has been accomplished by me as it truly ought to be; therefore, O Rāghavas, I wish further to build a bridge of dharma.
t.7.74.4: Together with you two, who are my very self, I wish to perform the unsurpassed Rājasūya sacrifice, for in it lies eternal dharma.
t.7.74.5: Mitra, the destroyer of foes, having sacrificed with the Rājasūya, a well-performed sacrifice with well-offered oblations, attained the state of Varuṇa.
t.7.74.6: And Soma, knower of dharma, having performed the Rājasūya sacrifice in accordance with dharma, attained fame among all the worlds and an everlasting abode.
t.7.74.7: Let whatever is best on this day be considered together with me. You two, being attentive, ought to speak what is beneficial and also conducive to future good.
t.7.74.8: Having heard these words of Rāghava, Bharata, skilled in speech, joined his palms in reverence and spoke these words.
t.7.74.9: In you, O virtuous one, supreme dharma is established; in you, O mighty-armed one, rests the whole earth, and in you too is fame, O you of boundless valor.
t.7.74.10: All the high-souled lords of the earth look up to you as the immortals look up to Prajāpati, just as we look upon you as the lord of the world.
t.7.74.11: And the people look upon you as a father, O king of great strength; you have become the refuge of all living beings on earth, O Rāghava.
t.7.74.12: How then will you, O king, perform such a sacrifice as this, in which the destruction of the royal lineages upon the earth is seen?
t.7.74.13: O king, all the men on earth who have attained manly valour will meet their destruction there, a destruction like that wrought by Death, the ender of all.
t.7.74.15: Having heard those words of Bharata, which were like nectar, Rāma, whose valour was true, obtained incomparable joy.
t.7.74.14: Therefore you, O tiger among men, whose valour is matched by none in virtues, ought not to destroy the earth, for it abides under your sway.
t.7.74.16: And he spoke these auspicious words to the one who increased Kaikeyī's joy: “I am pleased, I am truly gratified by your words today.”
t.7.74.17: O tiger among men, these manly words you have spoken, steeped in dharma, serve the protection of the earth.
t.7.74.18: Here I turn back from that intention, from the Rājasūya, the best of sacrifices, O knower of dharma, because of your well-spoken words.
t.7.74.19: The protection of the subjects is the dharma of kings, equal in measure to a sacrifice. Therefore I heed your words, well spoken and thoroughly considered.
